name: Library service administration
one_line: J-DEPTH placeholder template for the service side of running a library: the bibliographic and holdings record of the stock, the circulation and membership record of who borrowed what, the programming record of what was run in the building, and the service-performance return the authority files about itself. It is not activated by the word library, by a library's name, by a book title, or by a downloaded catalogue record of something the user is reading. Its distinct default against the government schema is two-part: a content-structural detector (labelled bibliographic and item/circulation slot structures that no other government sibling produces) and a privacy rule the schema default does not state — the patron-to-title link is the sensitive fact, so a borrower's reading may never become a display label or a folder level even where the person is already known. It declares no government field rows and no folder dimensions under PR-6, so activation unlocks only recognition, safety posture, universal facts, and grouping.

deterministic: PRECONDITION: these are template-activation signals on a fieldless schema, not licences to write government facts. Every accepted signal must evidence the corpus holder on the SERVICE side — running stock, membership, circulation, programming, or the service's own performance return — not reading, borrowing, citing, or visiting a library.

BIBLIOGRAPHIC TRANSFER STRUCTURE: a record whose internal structure is a bibliographic exchange format rather than prose — an ISO 2709 leader followed by a length-prefixed directory of numeric field tags, or an XML tree whose elements are record / leader / controlfield / datafield with numeric tag attributes and subfield codes. The structure is the signal; the titles inside it are not.

HOLDINGS-AND-ITEM SLOT PAIR: a labelled item-level slot holding a shelf-classification-shaped string beside a labelled item-barcode-shaped slot, repeated down a list. Neither half alone: a classification-shaped number on its own is a decimal, and a barcode-shaped digit run on its own is a stock or asset tag from any inventory.

CIRCULATION LEDGER STRUCTURE: labelled loan-transaction slots co-occurring in one row — an item identifier, a borrower identifier, and a loan-lifecycle slot (issue, due, return, renewal, hold, reservation, overdue). The lifecycle slot is what separates this from a plain stock inventory, which has quantities but no borrower and no due date.

MEMBERSHIP ADMINISTRATION SIDE: a membership application, card issue, or borrower-record maintenance document held with the ISSUING service's own form structure and internal reference — not a card a person keeps.

STOCK LIFECYCLE ON THE SELECTION SIDE: an acquisition, approval-plan, standing-order, donation-accession, stocktake, or withdrawal/weeding list carrying supplier or fund slots beside item identifiers, produced by the service that owns the shelves.

SERVICE PERFORMANCE RETURN: a labelled statistical return about the service's own operation — service points, opening hours, visits, active borrowers, issues, stock additions and withdrawals — submitted upward under a named return or collection cycle. The service is the RESPONDENT here, which is what keeps it out of the statistical-authority sibling.

PROGRAMMING AND OUTREACH ADMINISTRATION: a booking, registration, risk-assessment, or attendance record for an activity run IN a service point (reading challenge, class visit, rhyme time, digital-skills session, mobile-library route), where the venue is the corpus holder's own service point rather than a place the user attended.

INTERLENDING WORKFLOW: a request or supply record carrying a lending-request reference, a requesting-library and supplying-library pair, and a bibliographic citation — the two-library pair is what distinguishes it from a citation a researcher saved.
needs_llm: Distinguishing a committee agenda pack ABOUT the library service (municipal governance evidence, library only as subject) from a service-run operational document (this template's evidence). The governance-cycle structure decides it, not the word library.
Distinguishing a bibliographic export the service produced from a bibliographic export a researcher downloaded from a catalogue to feed a reference manager — identical file structure, opposite roles.

Deciding whether a withdrawal list is stock weeding (this template) or a records-disposal schedule (archives) or a collection deaccession (museum), when the list itself carries only identifiers and dates.
Reading a service-point screenshot far enough to tell an operational queue from a public-catalogue search result, without extracting the patron names visible on it.
Judging whether a mixed consultation packet about library closures belongs to the consultation proceeding or to the service's own operating record.
never_alone: The path or filename token 'Library' is not evidence of this template and is usually not even a document: the design already excludes it as a scan-time directory name — “The engine should ignore node_modules, .git, venv, build, dist, target, vendor, Pods, site-packages, Library, __pycache__, build artifacts, caches, auto-save folders, previews, and generated dependency trees.” A macOS user's home contains that directory; a library service is not implied by it.

A library's NAME (Central Library, County Library Service, a university library) is an organisation name and is never-alone evidence. The design forbids a template that would “use an author or organization merely as a collector”, and a service name in a header is exactly a collector.

A book, author, publisher, ISBN-shaped or ISSN-shaped token alone. That is a bibliographic citation, which appears in reading material, research bibliographies, invoices and shop confirmations far more often than in a service record.
A shelf-classification-shaped decimal alone. The same shape is a version string, a section number, a price, and a paragraph reference.
A digit-run barcode alone. Every inventory, asset register, warehouse manifest, and retail stock list has one.

The words catalogue, collection, holdings, accession, circulation, loan, renewal, or overdue as bare vocabulary. Each has a dominant non-library sense (product catalogue, photo collection, financial holdings, museum accession, banking circulation, credit loan, subscription renewal, overdue invoice).
A due date alone. It is the single most common labelled date slot in billing.
A person's name beside a title is not authorisation to write a reading fact; it is the reason this material is protected.
Absence of a governance block is not proof that a library-subject document is operational rather than committee material.

proposed_context_terms: PROPOSED for R6, not design: circulation, borrower record, holdings, shelfmark, accession, withdrawal, interlending, service point, active borrowers, issues per head. Each is proposed only as a CONTEXT term that must co-occur with a labelled slot structure; none may fire alone, and 00 lists none of them.

template.why: Empty by contract, and this row cannot differ from its schema here: PR-6 leaves the government schema fieldless, and a template may only branch on a field its schema declares, so there is no legal level to order. The structure this world wants remains prose until canonical adjudication: service function or bounded lifecycle first (stock, membership and circulation, programming, performance), then the exact collection, service point, programme, or return cycle, then the document's function. Two levels are affirmatively ruled out rather than deferred: a borrower must never become a dimension, and a title or shelf classification must never become a dimension, because either would publish a person's reading on the filesystem. Time is not first because “For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders.” Whatever order is later adjudicated stays editable, because “The system recommends an order based on the domain template, but the user can reverse, remove, add, or flatten dimensions.”

collides_with.signal: Shared fixture: Libraries and Culture Committee - Agenda Pack - 12 May 2026.pdf. Both worlds hold library-subject material produced by the same authority. This template requires service-operational structure (stock, item, borrower, programme, or performance slots); municipal administration owns the governance cycle (numbered agenda items, officer reports, minutes, resolutions) whatever the subject is. Library as SUBJECT goes to municipal; library as OPERATOR comes here.

Shared fixture: Weeding list - withdrawn stock 2026-Q2.csv. Both hold lists of things being removed. Archives requires a retention or disposal schedule reference and a records series; this template requires item barcodes and stock-condition or low-issue reasons. A digitisation batch of local-studies material sits on the seam and needs the same discriminator applied to its manifest.

Shared fixture family: accession and deaccession lists, condition and stocktake records. Museum collection requires an accession register entry with provenance and object description; this template requires circulating-stock structure — copies, barcodes, shelf classification, loan lifecycle. A rare-books or local-studies collection inside a library service is the genuinely contested case and is left to evidence, not to the holder's name.

Shared fixture: Stock selection meeting - approvals - August 2026.docx and the supplier framework behind it. Procurement owns the notice, specification, received bid, evaluation and award structure on the buying side; this template owns title-level selection against a fund, which is stock management even when a framework supplier is named. A library-management-system tender is procurement's, not this row's.

Shared fixture: Annual return - public library statistics 2025-26.xlsx. The statistical sibling holds the collecting authority's cycle — instruction, instrument, microdata, release. This template holds the same instrument on the RESPONDENT side, where the corpus holder is the service filing about itself. The bytes can be identical; the role slot decides.

Shared fixture: Library strategy consultation - responses export.zip. A shared consultation identifier across content-incoherent members is the consultation row's own grouping evidence. This template takes only the service's operational contribution to it (service-point data, opening-hours schedules), never the response corpus.

Shared fixture family: a university library's catalogue export, circulation report and membership record. The structures are identical to a public service's. Where the corpus holder is the institution, the institution's governance row holds it; where the corpus holder is a standalone public library service, this row does. Roster placement under government does not settle a university library, and that is recorded as an open question rather than decided here.

Shared fixture family: supplier invoices, stocktake sheets, staffing rotas, an inventory with barcodes. A bookshop's, a publisher's, or a company's internal knowledge-centre records have the same barcode-and-supplier shape. This template requires a public library service exercising a public function; a commercial holder's stock record stays business operations however book-shaped it is.

Shared fixture family: programme plans, attendance registers, volunteer rotas, funder reports for a reading campaign. A charity-run or community-managed library produces exactly these. Where the holder is a charity accounting to its board and funders, nonprofit holds it; where the holder is the statutory service, this row does. Neither is decided by the building.

Shared fixture family: copyright declarations on interlending forms, licence agreements for electronic resources, and requests for borrower data. Legal owns the executed agreement and the person's legal record; this template owns the operational form the declaration sits on. A subpoena or disclosure request for borrowing history is legal's document and this row's protected data, and must not be filed by what it discloses.

falls_through_to.when: a standalone service notice, opening-hours schedule, published stock policy, statistical return copy, or programme flyer has durable value but no accepted service-side workflow or group
falls_through_to.design_cite: Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.

falls_through_to.when: any borrower, membership, interlending, fines, staff-side queue, or borrowing-history material lacks a safe accepted group — the default outcome for this row's person-linked half
falls_through_to.design_cite: Protected Records may represent sensitive isolated material such as passport scans, medical documents, account statements, visas, legal forms, or credentials; it should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts.

falls_through_to.when: a sector report, professional article, or saved PDF is ABOUT libraries rather than produced by running one
falls_through_to.design_cite: Reading Inbox may hold papers, articles, reports, and saved PDFs that appear to be reading material but have no active research, course, or project association.

falls_through_to.when: a bibliographic transfer file or system dump is structurally unreadable to the extractor and carries no readable service context
falls_through_to.design_cite: Unsupported or Encrypted may hold—or, more safely, represent without moving—password-protected archives, unreadable documents, damaged files, and unknown formats.

sensitivity_why: This row's operational half is a record of what named people read, which is a stronger disclosure than the identity of the person alone: the borrower-to-title pair is the sensitive fact, and it appears in overdue reports, holds queues, interlending requests, fines ledgers and staff-screen captures. Membership applications carry dates of birth, addresses, proof-of-address evidence and guardian consent, including for children. Programme registers name attendees. The government schema's default already protects casework and submissions; this row adds the rule that the CONTENT of a loan may never become a display label or a folder level even where the person is already known, because the design requires that protected material “should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts.” The bibliographic half is genuinely public-facing, but its presence cannot lower the posture of a mixed export.
open_question: NEEDS-JOSEPH: (1) The row is fieldless under PR-6, and the two facts this world is saturated with — an item/bibliographic identifier and a borrower identifier — are deliberately NOT proposed as keys, because the first would immediately raise whether a title may be a folder level (answer here: no) and the second is the protected half of a disclosure pair. If PR-6 lifts, adjudicate centrally, not in this child. (2) Roster placement puts library administration under government, but academic, corporate and charity-run libraries produce byte-identical catalogue and circulation records; decide whether this row is holder-scoped to statutory public services with the others collided out (its current reading), or whether it is a cross-schema situation that government merely hosts. (3) Decide which sibling owns a rare-books or local-studies collection held inside a library service: this row, government.museum-collection, or government.archives-recordkeeping.
